chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Daylami, from his father, who said:
I asked Aba Abdillah عليه السلام about a well beside which there is a latrine, and he said to me:

‘Indeed, the course of all springs runs with the direction of the north wind. So if the clean well is above the north side and the latrine is lower than it, it does not harm it when there are cubits between them. But if the latrine is above the clean well, then it should be no less than twelve cubits. And if they are opposite one another in line with the qiblah, while both are level in the direction of the north wind, then seven cubits.’

key_terms.اثْنَيْ عَشَرَ ذِرَاعًا: a distance of twelve cubits required in one case
key_terms.النَّظِيفَةُ: the clean well, meaning the uncontaminated source of water
key_terms.الْبِئْرِ: the well whose purity and safety are being discussed
key_terms.الْقِبْلَةِ: the qiblah direction, used here to describe alignment
key_terms.الْكَنِيفُ: the latrine located near the well
key_terms.سَبْعَةُ أَذْرُعٍ: a distance of seven cubits required in another case
key_terms.مَجْرَى الْعُيُونِ: the course or flow of underground water sources
key_terms.مَهَبِّ الشَّمَالِ: the direction of the north wind, used here as a spatial indicator for water flow

ai.seo_question: What distance should separate a well and a latrine according to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling about the required distance between a well and a nearby latrine in order to protect the water from contamination. It explains different rulings based on relative elevation and directional flow, showing practical attention to taharah and the safeguarding of usable water.
